To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fish oil feeding is associated with a lower plasma cholesterol concentration and a lower binding affinity of LDL for rat liver plasma membranes.

fish oil diet increases the binding affinity of LDL for liver plasma membranes, and that changes of binding affinity induced in vitro by changes of lipoprotein and membrane source, support the importance of lipoprotein-lipid and membrane-lipid composition in binding studies.
the higher binding affinity observed in fish oil fed rats might be partly responsible for the hypolipidemic effect of marine oils as compared to saturated fat diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of dietary fatty acid on the binding of rat liver plasma membrane to LDL.

the study of the binding affinity of LDL from fish oil diet to rat liver plasma membranes, and the possible relationship between the hypocholesterolremic action of fish oil and the LDL receptor activity.
the effect of diet rich in saturated or polyunsaturated fatty acids on the LDL binding to rat liver plasma membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LDL binding to rat liver plasma membranes is influenced by diet, by the chemical composition of lipoproteins and by that of liver membranes.
the binding affinity of LDL from fish oil fed animals to liver plasma membranes from the same animals is higher than LDL binding affinity to liver plasma membranes of control and coconut oil rats.
fish oil and coconut oils, when given as a diet for four weeks, induce different modifications in liver plasma membranes composition, LDL and LDL binding to liver membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypocholesterolomic effect of fish oil feeding is related to the changes in the LDL and membrane composition and to the higher affinity of LDL to the liver plasma membrane.
the hypocholesterolomic action of fish oil diet is associated with changes of the LDL receptor binding activity.
fish oil diet increases the affinity of LDL for rat liver plasma membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LDL receptor activity is enhanced by fish oil diet.
the LDL binding affinity is higher for fish oil LDL than for coconut oil LDL, but the Bmax is similar for both.
the fatty acid composition of the liver plasma membrane and LDL is an important factor in the binding affinity of LDL for the liver plasma membrane.
